newsitem.title: USA: China central banker says China to defend HK dlr.
newsitem.headline: China central banker says China to defend HK dlr.

text.p: Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China Chen Yuan said on Friday the Chinese central bank will support the stability of the Hong Kong dollar after the July 1 transfer of sovereignty over the British colony.

"We are prepared to provide liquidity to support for the purpose of stabilizing the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar at the request of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority," Chen told a seminar on Hong Kong's future hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

"The People's Bank of China will provide support for maintaining currency stability in Hong Kong," said Chen, who reaffirmed the often-stated principles of "one country, two systems" and "two currencies and two monetary systems."

Chen reminded the audience of bankers and economists that the Hong Kong dollar will remain the "only legal tender in Hong Kong... freely convertible," pegged to the U.S. dollar at the current fixed exchange rate.
Chen also repeated that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will be responsible for the stability of the Hong Kong dollar and Hong Kong's financial markets.
However, the People's Bank of China and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to cooperate closely while remaining independent from each other.

Chen also stressed the importance of "the complementarity between Shanghai and Hong Kong," mainly because "in the short run, and at least before the renminbi becomes fully convertible, Shanghai does not possess the prerequisites to become an international financial center."

New York Fed President William McDonough, who delivered the opening remarks of the seminar, described the transfer of sovereignty of the British colony to China as "essentially a political event, but with financial implications."
"The markets made it clear it (transfer of sovereignty) will be a successful transition," McDonough said.
